registered: 2026-11-06 ~17:20 ET, before any data pull for this study.
operator: 2026-11-06 'yes' to weekend item 8 (backlog row 58a, from the 10/30 review): does a sudden tightening of the real spread mark the start of a run?
question: At the desk's arm, is the entry better when the real (SIP) spread tightened in the last minute than when it did not?
sample: Every desk entry (arm time t0 = the fill second) 2026-09-16 through 2026-11-05 with a fill row, split by date at the median day into EARLY and LATE halves. SIP quotes from t0 - 5 minutes to t0 (free historical).
measure: From SIP quotes with bid > 0 and ask > bid: s_recent = median quoted spread (bp of mid) over [t0 - 60 s, t0); s_before = median over [t0 - 300 s, t0 - 60 s). ratio = s_recent / s_before. COMPRESSED = ratio <= 0.70 with at least 20 quotes in each window; fewer quotes = not measurable (counted, excluded).
outcome: The desk's actual net bp per trade (exit vs entry, less 3 bp) and the never-green label, from outcomes.jsonl.
statistic: Per day: mean net of COMPRESSED entries minus mean net of the other measurable entries, for days with both. Mean over days, day-clustered t.
pass: STRONG, ALL of: (1) mean day difference > 0 with t >= 2.0; (2) > 0 in BOTH halves; (3) COMPRESSED entries have mean net > 0 in BOTH halves (a gate that only keeps them must make money); (4) at least 60 COMPRESSED entries in each half.
fail: Any condition missing = FAIL. No other ratio cutoff or window is scored as primary.
information_only: the same measure 5 minutes AFTER the fill (is a widening spread an early warning?)
if_pass: result-skeptic review; live use needs REAL-TIME quotes (the paid SIP plan), so a pass is shelved until SIP; replay through sweep_replays first.
tool: tools/studies/spread_compression.py (built after this file is committed)
